# Rule index: java

Every rule ID of the java docs with its headline, grouped by doc. The headline is the rule's first sentence; the full rule (details, values, examples, *Why*) is in the doc. **Before you implement against a rule, read its full text**: search the doc for the ID and read that bullet, or read the doc when the task is centred on its topic. MUST = deviation needs an ADR; SHOULD = default, deviate with a stated reason; no keyword = MUST unless it says *prefer*, *default* or *consider*.

## [Java: Hexagonal Architecture](../05-building-block-view/java.md)

- JAVA-ARCH-01: Package-private is the default visibility.
- JAVA-ARCH-02: Sub-packages break package-private.
- JAVA-ARCH-03: Commands, queries, results and value objects are `record`s that validate in the compact constructor (the Java mechanism for ARCH-UC-05).
- JAVA-ARCH-04: ARCH-UC-06 in Java is the canonical record constructor; no builders for commands.
- JAVA-ARCH-05: Bean Validation (`jakarta.validation`) is optional for declarative checks on commands.
- JAVA-ARCH-06: Domain entities protect their invariants.
- JAVA-ARCH-07: Every project has an ArchUnit test class (JUnit Jupiter) that checks the dependency table from 05-building-block-view/code-organization.md.
- JAVA-ARCH-08: Never disable `archRule.failOnEmptyShould` (enabled by default in current ArchUnit versions).
- JAVA-ARCH-09: Build modules are split once the architecture is stable, in the order of ARCH-ENF-06.
- JAVA-ARCH-10: Dependencies between modules are declared explicitly in the build file and reviewed (ARCH-ENF-07).
- JAVA-ARCH-11: A plain-Java application wires everything in one place:
- JAVA-ARCH-12: Invalid input throws one dedicated exception from `domain` (the validation category of ARCH-UC-13) (e.g. `DomainValidationException extends RuntimeException`, carrying a stable error code and, where known, the field).
- JAVA-ARCH-13: Each business error category of ARCH-UC-13 has one abstract base type in `domain`:
- JAVA-ARCH-14: Time comes from one `java.time.Clock` bean, and ArchUnit bans every other source of the current time (ARCH-UC-20).

## [Java Tooling](../08-crosscutting-concepts/development/java-tooling.md)

- JAVA-TOOL-01: Java 25 (LTS).
- JAVA-TOOL-02: The Maven Wrapper is committed (`mvnw`, `mvnw.cmd`, `.mvn/wrapper/`).
- JAVA-TOOL-03: Maven 3.9.9 or newer (enforcer range `[3.9.9,)`).
- JAVA-TOOL-04: The JDK version is documented and enforced.
- JAVA-TOOL-05: Every version lives in `<properties>` or the BOM.
- JAVA-TOOL-06: The enforcer bans what the baseline forbids:
- JAVA-TOOL-07: Error Prone and NullAway run in every compile, in JSpecify mode, restricted to `@NullMarked` code.
- JAVA-TOOL-08: Every package is `@NullMarked` (`package-info.java` with `org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked`), container packages without classes (`adapter`, `adapter.in`, `ports`) included;
- JAVA-TOOL-09: Generated code is excluded from Error Prone (`-XepExcludedPaths`), Spotless and SpotBugs.
- JAVA-TOOL-10: `.mvn/jvm.config` carries the `--add-exports`/`--add-opens` flags Error Prone needs on a modern JDK (file in the templates).
- JAVA-TOOL-11: Spotless formats Java with palantir-java-format (120 columns, like Prettier in the frontend), removes unused imports and orders the rest.
- JAVA-TOOL-12: SpotBugs runs with FindSecBugs in `verify` and fails on findings reported at `threshold` `Medium` or higher.
- JAVA-TOOL-25: XML, XSL-FO, SVG and HTML built in Java are written through a writer API, never by string concatenation, even with escaped values:
- JAVA-TOOL-13: PMD and Checkstyle are not part of the baseline.
- JAVA-TOOL-14: JaCoCo produces a report, not a gate (D5, TEST-ARCH-09).
- JAVA-TOOL-15: Mockito is attached as an explicit agent.
- JAVA-TOOL-16: Vulnerable dependencies are caught by a dependency scan in CI that fails a pull request on new findings at or above the gate's threshold (SEC-CI-01 and its gate table).
- JAVA-TOOL-17: An SBOM is produced in `verify` or the release job (`cyclonedx-maven-plugin`).
- JAVA-TOOL-18: Dependency updates are deliberate (merged after review, not automatically):
- JAVA-TOOL-23: Builds are reproducible.
- JAVA-TOOL-19: Unit tests are `*Test` (Surefire), integration tests `*IT` (Failsafe).
- JAVA-TOOL-20: Every Java component offers the same commands, run from the component folder (REPO-TOOL-03), so humans, agents and CI don't have to guess:
- JAVA-TOOL-24: Before the commit, all gate findings are collected in one run, without ignoring any.
- JAVA-TOOL-21: A SAST tool runs in CI next to FindSecBugs with an agreed rule set (SEC-CI-01, secure-pipeline.md;
